summary: Comprehensive frontend validation of the lockdown-persistence, idempotency, leaderboard, reorder and customer-profile enhancements requested in the review. 8/9 scenarios PASS. One BLOCKER found on SM Dashboard — the '🏆 Leaderboard' tab exists but its <TabsContent value="leaderboard"> is not wired, so the panel never renders for the Sales Manager (works fine on TC + Admin). Also noted: React state-based idempotency guard is vulnerable to same-microtask synchronous JS clicks (unusual but still a real race in slow-network re-renders).

ui_bugs.issue: 🏆 Leaderboard tab is declared in TabsList (v:'leaderboard') and TelecallerLeaderboardPanel is imported (line 36) BUT there is NO <TabsContent value="leaderboard">…</TabsContent> block, so clicking the tab shows a blank area. Query for [data-testid="tc-leaderboard"] returns null on SM. Fix: add `<TabsContent value="leaderboard" className="animate-fade-in"><TelecallerLeaderboardPanel role="telecaller" /></TabsContent>` alongside the tcperf/leads content blocks.

State-based `if (savingCallLog) return;` guard is not truly race-safe. When 3 clicks fire in the same JS microtask (e.g. b.click();b.click();b.click() or a fast custom bridging event), all three see savingCallLog=false because React state hasn't flushed. Realistic 50ms-spaced clicks are correctly blocked because the button becomes disabled after re-render, but a pathological synchronous burst fires 3 PUT /api/leads. Fix: additionally guard via a `useRef` synchronous boolean (savingRef.current) that is set immediately before the await. Same applies to creatingOrder.

rca of the issue: SM Leaderboard tab missing panel: developer added tab entry + import statement but forgot the TabsContent block. Radix Tabs simply renders no children when no matching TabsContent value is found — no error thrown, silent blank state. Idempotency race: React setState is asynchronous; three synchronous clicks in the same microtask all see the stale `savingCallLog=false` closure. The disabled prop on the button prevents further human clicks only after React re-renders. Programmatic burst clicks or extremely fast native double-click firing within one animation frame can slip through. useRef provides a synchronous mutable latch that closes this gap.
